The results are intended to be used to help orient and adapt the follow-on development activity with respect to various aspects (i.e. technical, implementation, cost, etc.).Description:When examining new applications of existing technologies (i.e. already used in space or coming from other sectors) or new technologies, there are often questions to resolve about the most promising application and the actual potential added value or performance of the technology (as compared to the state-of-the art). There are also sometimes questions about the potential adaptation effort required or the feasibility of dealing with the environment conditions of Space.Although it is not possible to address all potential questions, it is relevant to address the most critical issues to make an assessment and provide orientation before embarking on a full technology development. In addition, by addressing these issues, it also possible to shape the full development activity with respect to a targeted application, to refine the associated specifications and work programme and to help dimension the cost and the schedule. The assessments for potential development activities are intended to provide a better understanding of the potential advantages of a given technology for a given application and to address critical issues (i.e. to help mitigate risks with respect to a future development activity).Activities will typically include at least one of the following tasks: Identification and analysis of specifications for one or more space applications and the technical assessment of the development actions and associated schedule and cost. Assessment of the potential benefits (performance, cost, lead time, risks...) and disadvantages of the potentiallution with respect to the state-of-the-art. Assessment of potential critical issues related to using a given technology for a specific application, using analysis/simulation and/or breadboarding and testing. Define the full development activity with respect to a targeted application, refining the associated specifications and work programme and estimating the cost and establishing the schedule.The de-risk framework is targeted to develop generic technology but will also cover dedicated initiatives to boost specific technologies (e.g. AI, Energy systems, propulsion systems, Quantum technology, Advance manufacturing, etc.) and to support established companies to improve their products portfolio with a longer term development. In particular, this framework covers the first stepof the product portfolio initiative. This initiative aims to strength medium entities, with already established experience in termsof developing products, to maintaining a product family and intend to expand the sales of their products beyond present opportunities.The maximum amount per activity is 250 k.
